title: WPSS/1590/2020 of JYOTI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No.1590 of 2020
Jyoti ........Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others .....Respondents
Presence:-
Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)

Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. By means of this writ petition, petitioner has
challenged the order dated 05.09.2020, passed by
respondent no.3, annexure-1 to the writ petition, whereby
the petitioner was not given approval for her appointment
on the post of Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade (English) on
the ground that on the date of sanction of the post i.e. on
20.02.2014 and when the Institution was brought in
grant-in-aid on 01.02.2016, petitioner was not having the
compulsory essential qualification of UTET-II/CTET-II and
further commanding the respondents to absorb the
petitioner as Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade with the
respondent-Institution.
3. The facts which are not in dispute are that the
petitioner was appointed as Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade
(English) pursuant to advertisement dated 04.01.2013
with the respondent no.4-Saraswati Vidhya Mandir,
Kanakpal Janta Higher Secondary School, Quidang Kothi,
Nailchami, Bhilangna, District Tehri Garhwal, a Non-Government Un-aided Institution by then. The

2
appointment of the petitioner was made by respondent
no.4 subject to submission of B.Ed degree within one year
and accordingly, the petitioner joined on the post of
Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade (English) on 22.05.2013.
The Committee of the Management forwarded the
selection of the petitioner for approval to the Chief
Education Officer, Tehri Garhwal-respondent no.3 on
25.07.2023 under the provisions of Uttarakhand School
Education Act, 2006 and Regulations framed there-under,
but when no approval was given by the respondent no.3,
petitioner was accorded approval by resorting to the
clause of deemed approval in the Rules. The petitioner
submitted her B.Ed mark-sheet and on its submission,
petitioner was given permanent status on 22.02.2014 and
the petitioner joined on permanent basis in the Institution
on 24.02.2014. On 26.02.2014, the Manager of the School
sent the matter of the petitioner for approval.
4. In between, the Institution was taken by the
State Government under grant-in-aid on 20.02.2014 and
the post of Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade has also been
sanctioned vide order dated 20.02.2014. The State
Government has passed the order for payment of salary-grant stating therein that the terms and conditions
stipulated in Government Order dated 01.02.2016 will be
applicable. The Management of the Institution on
02.02.2018 has requested the respondent no.3 to grant
financial approval to the appointment of the petitioner,
but vide impugned order dated 05.09.2020, the claim of
the petitioner for absorption on the post of Assistant
Teacher, L.T. Grade (English) has been rejected only on
the ground that the petitioner has not passed UTET-

3
II/CTET-II Examination compulsory qualification for
Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade.
5. It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner
has been appointed on the post of Assistant Teacher, L.T.
Grade on 22.05.2013 prior to the coming into force of new
Rules i.e. on 13.03.2014. Thus, the qualification which
was made compulsory qualification on 13.03.2014 cannot
be made applicable in case of the petitioner. It is pointed
case of the petitioner that the qualification cannot be
applied retrospectively.
6. It is contended by learned counsel for the
petitioner that in a similar controversy, the Co-ordinate
Bench of this Court in Writ Petition (S/S) No.3491 of 2018
(Mamta Sah vs. State of Uttarakhand & others) vide order
dated 02.03.2022 has allowed the writ petition and
directed the respondent in that writ petition to grant
approval to the appointment of the petitioner in that case
as Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade (General) in the light of
Amended Act No.24 of 2017 and w.e.f. 07.03.2017. He
further submits that the State Government feeling
aggrieved by the aforesaid order passed by the Co-ordinate
Bench of this Court took up the matter in the Special
Appeal No.385 of 2022 (State of Uttarakhand & others vs.
Mamta Sah & another), which too was disposed of vide
judgment and order dated 05.03.2024 and the judgment
impugned in the special appeal has not been disturbed.
7. It is also contended by learned counsel for the
petitioner that the controversy involved in the aforesaid
case is quite similar to the controversy involved in this
case, therefore, this writ petition may also be decided on
the same terms and conditions.

4
8. Learned State Counsel does not dispute the
similarity of the aforesaid case.
9. In this view of the matter, taking parity of the
aforesaid judgment and order dated 02.03.2022 passed by
the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court which is affirmed by
the Division Bench of this Court in Special Appeal vide
judgment and order dated 05.03.2024, the writ petition is
allowed in terms of the aforesaid judgment and order. The
impugned order dated 05.09.2020, passed by respondent
no.3 is hereby quashed. The petitioner is entitled to get
the approval and her claim for salary on regular pay scale
w.e.f. the date of her attaining the qualification of UTET-II/CTET-II.
10. No order as to costs.
11. All pending applications, if any, stand disposed
of.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 01.05.2024
AK
